summary: Colby, a liberal-arts college in Maine, charges no application fee to anyone and meets 100% of demonstrated need for every admitted student, including international students — with the chance to graduate without loans.
covers: No application fee for any applicant.
100% of demonstrated need met for admitted students, including international students.
Aid designed so that students can graduate without loans to repay.
eligibility: Colby is need-aware for international applicants: your aid request is considered in the admission decision.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application or QuestBridge.
Choose Early Decision I (15 November), Early Decision II (4 January) or Regular Decision (4 January).
Submit the CSS Profile and Colby's international financial documents by the aid deadlines.
Early Decision applicants hear about a month after the deadline.
watch_out: Early Decision rounds are binding — ED II lets you commit after an early rejection elsewhere.
As a need-aware college for internationals, Colby admits a limited number of aided international students each year.
Colby is in a small town in Maine; winters are long and cold.

Optional: a video interview through Duolingo, Vericant or InitialView

faq.q: Can I apply for aid after I am admitted?
faq.a: Don't wait. If you do not complete Colby's aid application before admission, you cannot receive Colby grants for two years, unless your family's finances change in a way nobody could have expected.

faq.q: Do I have to send SAT or ACT scores?
faq.a: No. Colby lists test scores among its optional materials.
No. Colby meets 100% of demonstrated need with grants and a campus job. Some families choose to borrow towards their own contribution, but that is their choice.
